assertions.name: two_I_burnside_check
assertions.source: Σ dim² over 2I irreps = |2I| = 120 (Burnside); verifies the affine Ê_8 Coxeter mark list (1,2,3,4,5,6,4,3,2) is the correct 2I irrep dim spectrum.

assertions.name: a5_burnside_check
assertions.source: Σ dim² over A_5 irreps = |A_5| = 60 (Burnside); matches the irrep dim list (1,3,3,4,5) used in T4.

assertions.name: klein_orbit_sum_matches_riemann_hurwitz_signature
assertions.source: Klein orbit triple 12 + 20 + 30 = 62 (NOT |A_5| = 60).  The orbits are |G|/|stab| with stabs 5, 3, 2 respectively; 62 = 60·(1/5 + 1/3 + 1/2) = 60·(31/30) = 62. This is the Riemann-Hurwitz signature of the icosahedral covering of the orbifold P¹(2,3,5).  Renamed from `klein_orbit_sum_equals_group_order` (Copilot review) since the value differs from |A_5|.

description: GAP-A-4 T9 — scaffold for Klein-invariant / McKay-E_8 / Bring direction.  After T5–T8 refuted 5 q-Schur / RT candidates, T9 sets up the non-Schur-Weyl alternative: tabulates the 2I/Ê_8 irrep dims + Klein degree triple (12,20,30) + queues 3 concrete open sub-questions (T10 McKay-character / T11 Klein-J / T12 Bring-discriminant).  NO derivation proposed here — formalize-first discipline prohibits a 6th ansatz.

open_subquestions.name: McKay-character h⁴ candidate
open_subquestions.question: Does the 2I → A_5 → H restriction (dim-5 irrep of 2I passing to dim-5 irrep H of A_5) have a natural h-expansion whose h⁴ coefficient is −3/4 via the 2I-character orthogonality evaluated at a q-deformed argument?  The Ê_8 Coxeter marks (1,2,3,4,5,6,4,3,2) might encode the h⁴ structure as a characteristic-class invariant.
open_subquestions.tractability: Medium. 2I character table is classical (9×9); q-deforming is a finite-dim problem.  Tractable in ≤ 200 lines pure mpmath.

open_subquestions.name: Klein J-invariant h-expansion
open_subquestions.question: Does the icosahedral J-invariant J = T² / H³ have a natural expansion in a q-deformed Klein coordinate whose leading h-correction is −3/4? J is a degree-0 rational function on ℂP¹/I with three critical values 0, 1, ∞ matching the three icosahedral orbit types — the universal h⁴ might emerge from the J ↦ q-twist analogue of the Riemann-Hurwitz formula.
open_subquestions.tractability: High. Klein invariants are explicit polynomials; the syzygy T² + H³ = 1728·f⁵ is closed form; q-deformation is well-defined via formal Taylor series.  ~300 lines pure mpmath.

open_subquestions.name: Bring quintic discriminant h⁴
open_subquestions.question: Does the Bring quintic surface's discriminant (the locus in ℂP⁴ where the quintic degenerates) have a natural h-expansion under a q-deformation tied to substrate q_0 whose first non-trivial coefficient is −3/4? The Bring surface is the universal covering of ℂP¹ \ {0, 1, ∞} with A_5 monodromy — its discriminant carries icosahedral characteristic-class information.
open_subquestions.tractability: Lower. Bring quintic computations are involved (~600+ lines or external resolvent); requires careful symbolic setup.

data.synthesis_verdict: T9 sets up the non-Schur-Weyl direction structurally without proposing a derivation.  The dim-5 irrep H of A_5 sits at the unique dim-5 node of affine Ê_8 in the McKay correspondence — a canonical position that the q-Schur picture (T8 refuted) does not see.  The Klein degree triple (12, 20, 30) encodes the icosahedral orbit structure on ℂP¹ via (|G|/stab) for the three special orbit types (vertices, faces, edges).  Three concrete follow-up sub-questions are queued: T10 (McKay-character h⁴ via 2I), T11 (Klein J-invariant h-expansion — highest tractability), T12 (Bring quintic discriminant). Per formalize-first discipline, NO derivation of h⁴ = −3/4 is claimed here — that would be the 6th ansatz the discipline review catches.  T9 just tabulates the canonical icosahedral data and pins the open questions.
